messages:
alex: heads-up — dug into the recent P99 regressions and I think we have a subtle interaction between the per-request offload budget and our NUMA-aware allocator.
priya: short version?
ajex: (typo) alex: TL;DR: short-lived KV cache entries get pinned on the local NUMA node, then a big sequence request triggers eviction pressure that prefers remote-node staged pages, which fragments the local pool and forces async offload to host. P99 goes up.
priya: ah ok. are we seeing this only for bursty long-seq requests?
alex: mostly. traces show pattern: many small inferences allocate tiny KV slices -> mark as resident -> freed soon, but our allocator's freelist normalization lumps them into small slabs on node A. When a burst long request appears on node A it needs large contiguous residency and ends up moving things to host from node B first because of our per-node scoring.
jamie: can you paste the scoring code you mean?
alex: sure — it's basically: 

```
score(page) = base_age * age_weight + resident_size * size_weight + remote_penalty(node_diff)
if score > threshold -> consider offload
```

We introduced a hard remote_penalty to avoid cross-node reads, but that backfires under fragmentation.
priya: so remote_penalty encourages dropping remote pages first which is fine, but if local is tiny fragmented, we should prefer coalescing local slabs over shipping remote pages out.
ciara: two axes: (1) choose which pages to offload, (2) whether to proactively coalesce/defragment before offloading. We only do the former.
jamie: defrag at runtime sounds expensive. maybe we should bias the scoring toward eviction candidates that will free contiguous address space e.g., prefer freeing adjacent pages owned by same slab.
theo: we could add a locality bonus: if candidate pages are adjacent or belong to same slab, reduce effective fragmentation metric. but detecting that adds per-candidate lookups.
priya: what about a staged heuristic: cheap check for slab adjacency (O(1) from slab header), if adjacency_count > k then bonus. fallback to current scoring otherwise.
ciara: also consider request-level hints: for long-seq requests mark them as "contiguous_residency_needed" — runtime can try opportunistic coalescing in background before offload. if request finishes early, cancel.
jamie: request hints sound good but we need API boundary: model callers shouldn't have to specify. infer-controller can classify by token_budget (if > X treat as long).
theo: agree. also think about changing remote_penalty to be dynamic: factor in current fragmentation metric F_local. remote_penalty = base_remote_penalty * (1 - min(1, F_local / F_thresh)). so if local highly fragmented, remote_penalty reduces.
alex: nice — that lets us still prefer local under normal conditions. we need to define F_local: maybe fraction of free runs >= run_length_needed? we can estimate needed run_length by looking at active requests' max_seq.
priya: complexity aside, can we prototype with a simulator on top of current residency sampler? jamie — can you add flags to evictbot to sample F_local and log decisions?
jamie: yep, will add a /evictbot sample-frag and sample-decision dump.
evictbot: bot: created job evict-sample-196450 for node A/B — will collect 5k decision traces.
ciara: also think about reclamation latency: coalescing can add latency upfront. background coalesce with soft-preempt should be default. only do sync coalesce when request explicitly needs contiguous space and deadline allows.
theo: edge case: pinned pages by user processes (private deployments) — we should reflect client pin hints (client-managed TTL) into scoring. priority: respect explicit pin TTL and avoid coalescing pinned slabs.
alex: good point. for private deployments we can expose a per-request residency_hint that flows down. for hosted, runtime inference-controller will infer.
priya: next steps: jamie adds evictbot sampling logs, theo implements dynamic remote_penalty prototype + adjacency bonus, ciara drafts a small RFC describing API for request residency_hint and background coalesce semantics. alex will run a few p99 simulations against dev cluster.
alex: thanks — let's aim for an RFC draft by EOD Friday. if anyone wants to jump on the prototype ping me. :raised_hands:
priya: tagging perf-checklist: we should measure both token latency and tail GC stalls.
jamie: noted. I'll push the sampling patch to canary tonight.
evictbot: bot: canary deploy queued — rolling to eng-runtime-canary in 3h.
